passage:
Grandma had a wooden mold for making moon cakes. It was old and dark from years of use.
Her grandson wanted to use a plastic mold because it was easier to clean. Grandma agreed to try it, but the moon cakes looked different. The designs were clear, yet something felt missing.
Then Grandma showed him how to press the dough into the wooden mold. It took more care, but the pattern came out beautifully.
She explained that her mother had used the same mold.
The grandson understood that tools can carry memory. A newer tool may be easier, but an old one can connect hands across generations.
